title: AI Is Fracking the Open Web
gist: Lucky Gunasekara argues that AI labs treat the open web like a coal seam to be mined by crawlers for model training, which breaks digital publishers' traditional ways of managing real and robust demand for their content; building an alternative will fall to the remaining open-web advocates.

themes.theme: Extractive AI crawling of the web

insights.claim: Frontier AI model builders, armed with GPUs and venture capital, treat the open web as a raw resource to be extracted by crawlers and fed into model training, much like mining a coal seam.
insights.speaker: LUCKY GUNASEKARA
insights.so_what: Frames the content-licensing fight: publishers' data is an input cost AI labs have historically not paid for, which is a liability/pricing risk for model builders.
insights.quote: the open web is a vast raw seam of informational material just waiting for someone with enough computing power and cleverness to release its potential
insights.locator: At some point in the AI race

insights.claim: Cyberspace is being inundated with bots designed to extract value wherever it can be found, making the old methods publishers used to manage demand for their content unworkable.
insights.speaker: LUCKY GUNASEKARA
insights.so_what: Traffic- and ad-based publishing models face structural pressure; watch bot-management, paywall, and content-licensing businesses as beneficiaries.
insights.locator: The demand for what digital publishers

insights.claim: Demand for what digital publishers offer remains real and robust even as AI bots disrupt the channels for monetizing it.
insights.speaker: LUCKY GUNASEKARA
insights.so_what: The problem is monetization plumbing, not relevance, so quality content owners with leverage (licensing deals, direct access) could reprice rather than disappear.
insights.quote: The demand for what digital publishers offer is real and robust
insights.locator: The demand for what digital publishers

insights.claim: Building an alternative to the extractive AI-crawler model will fall to the remaining advocates of the old open web.
insights.speaker: LUCKY GUNASEKARA
insights.so_what: Look for coalitions, protocols or standards from open-web advocates (access controls, paid crawling) as an emerging infrastructure niche.
